findings.claim: `import * as regexes from "./regexes.js"` is a runtime (value) import, unlike every other import in this file's header, which is type-only. This introduces a real module dependency from json-schema-processors into regexes and could create a circular import or unexpected bundle growth.
findings.rationale: All neighboring imports are `import type`, so this file previously had (almost) no runtime deps on the sibling modules. Adding a value import means regexes.js is now evaluated whenever this module loads. If regexes.js (or anything it transitively pulls in) imports back into the core schema graph, this can produce a TDZ/undefined-at-module-init problem that only manifests at runtime in certain bundlers. Worth confirming regexes.js is dependency-free and that the imported regex objects are only read lazily inside functions, not at module top level. Confidence: low-to-moderate — regexes.js is typically leaf-level in zod, so this is likely fine, but the asymmetry with the other imports is worth a second look.

findings.claim: Newly imported `type Seen` may be unused or may indicate the file now depends on internal to-JSON-Schema traversal state that it previously did not.
findings.rationale: The hunk only shows the import being added; if `Seen` is not actually referenced in the rest of the file, it is dead (harmless but noise under `noUnusedLocals`, which would fail the build). More importantly, if it *is* used, it means processors now reach into per-node traversal/cycle-tracking state — a behavior-relevant coupling worth verifying that callers pass a consistent `Seen` and that mutation of it doesn't leak across separate `toJSONSchema` invocations. Confidence: low, since the hunk doesn't show the usage site.
